card.title: COMMANDO RAID
card.text: Deal 1 damage. Add two No. 10 COMMANDO units to your support line.
card.flavorText: A notable example of a British commando raid during WWII was the Saint-Nazaire Raid, also known as Operation Chariot, which took place on March 28, 1942. The objective of the raid was to disable the heavily fortified dry dock at Saint-Nazaire, France, which was used for repairing and refitting German warships, particularly battleships and U-boats. By disabling the dry dock, the British hoped to disrupt German naval operations in the Atlantic and weaken their ability to threaten Allied shipping lanes. The raiding force, led by Commando units under the command of Lieutenant Colonel Charles Newman, included sailors from the Royal Navy, Royal Marines and Army commandos. The force embarked on the nighttime assault using a converted destroyer, HMS Campbeltown, which was packed with explosives and disguised to resemble a German vessel. Under the cover of darkness and a diversionary bombardment, the Campbeltown rammed the gates of the dry dock, which allowed the commandos to disembark and engage in fierce close combat with German defenders. Despite heavy casualties and intense resistance, the commandos succeeded in achieving their objective by detonating the explosives aboard the Campbeltown and rendering the dry dock unusable. Although the raid inflicted significant damage on the Saint-Nazaire port, it came at a high cost and many commandos were killed, wounded, or captured by the Germans.
